content.text:
I've written the migrated file and type checking passes for it. The only `tsc` errors are in the original `src/module.ts`, because lodash isn't installed. I haven't compared the output against lodash.

`out/module.ts` now imports `merge` from `es-toolkit`, and `startCase` and `truncate` from `es-toolkit/compat`.

- **`merge`:** the core es-toolkit version merges arrays by index and mutates `base`, as lodash does. That covers the input range, so I used it instead of the larger compat one.
- **`startCase`:** the core version lowercases the rest of each word. The input range allows consecutive capitals, so the core version would give a different result than lodash, for example `ABC` would become `Abc`. The compat version preserves the case and gave sensible results on a few test strings (`XML Http 2 Req` for `XMLHttp2Req`).
- **`truncate`:** this is only available in compat.
- **Lodash:** no lodash import remains.

**Size:** `npm run size -- out/module.ts` prints 2364 bytes (min+gzip) and 97 bytes of own code. A variant that used the compat `merge` as well came to 4044 bytes. I couldn't build the original for a baseline, so I can't say how the own-code bytes compare with it.

I didn't write any replacement utilities or adapters.
